title: Quaker Silence
summary: Modelled on a Quaker meeting for business. Agents sit in shared silence. An agent speaks only when it is moved (it has something new and important), speaks once per matter, and everyone listens. The Clerk does not vote or argue: it discerns the "sense of the meeting" and writes a minute that everyone can unite with.
whenToUse: Hard decisions where quick talk would drown quiet insight, or where token spend must stay low and every utterance should count.
strengths: Very little chatter: silence is the default
Each voice is heard in full
Unity instead of majority: minority views shape the minute
risks: An important voice may stay silent
Needs a skilled Clerk to read unity honestly

smileMetrics.cooperation: Contributions that changed the minute ÷ contributions made.
smileMetrics.harmony: Agents uniting with the minute (standing aside counts half).
smileMetrics.gathering: Rounds before the minute is agreed.

communication: Each round every Friend may speak or keep silence; whatever is spoken reaches all. After a round with no new ministry the Clerk proposes a minute, and the Friends answer with Unity.
cooperation: Cooperation = ministry that changed the minute ÷ ministry spoken. Silence costs nothing and is honoured.
